findings.text: `Server/rename-phase-to-step.mjs` breaks things if it is run a second time. Its own `--dry-run`, run today, would rewrite `body.step ?? body.phase` into `body.step ?? body.step` (Process.js:100), turn `{ step: _s, phase: _p }` into a duplicate `step` key (Process.js:102), and change the old-shape test line (ProcessRunner.test.mjs:44) so it no longer tests an old line. That would quietly remove the old-log alias the brief requires. Make the script refuse when `STEP_LINES` is already in Process.js, or skip lines that mention `body.phase` and `phase: _p`.

`Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md:19` gained the line the brief asked for, but the bullet in front of it still says "Multi-phase work… each phase's session… every phase". The page now uses both words; "phase" there should be "step".

`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:356` `CLASS_SOURCES.Process` still lists only `core/Task/Process.js`, so the class text read at line 389 no longer contains the templates (they now live in `processes/*.js`). Add `core/Task/processes/index.js` there if that text is meant to show what a Process can do.

The templates only exist when `processes/index.js` has been imported. Code that imports `Process.js` directly gets an empty `Process.TEMPLATES`, so `Process.lines({process:"build"})` returns null. The comment at Process.js:103 says this. Today page_tools loads index.js, so Servex works, but a browser page that imports Process.js and calls `template()` would find nothing.
There is no `session.jsonl` in the task folder yet, so the "Done means" items (review answers, the `ready:` line, `--status` clean) are still to do after this review.

The option name chosen is `steps_over` (Process.js:93; the brief allowed "steps_over or similar"). Nothing in the repo passed the old `phases:` override (the one other `phases:`, in `Server/refine.mjs:430`, is a different thing), so nothing broke. A caller still passing `phases` now gets it written onto line 1 as a plain field, with no error.
